catalog_quote: 2.2 超分節要素 ムラブリ語は超分節要素 (声調、強勢、母音の長短など) によって語彙を弁別しない。ただし、強勢は音韻語の境界を示す境界表示機能を担う。母音の長短も、常にではないが、強勢を持つ音節にのみ現れうるため、境界表示機能を一部担う。 2.3 音韻語 音韻語 1 つにつき、1 つの強勢を持つ。強勢位置は音韻語の最終音節である。 また、1 音韻語は必ず 2 モーラ以上 [fn. 1] であるとする、最小語制約が存在する。この制約の存在は、開音節の自由形式が長母音で発音されることから分かる。... 例 1 に示す例は全て 1 音韻語をなす。 (1) a. boP ["bo:P∼boP] 「乳」 b. goh ["goh]「折れる」 c. tmPoP [tm."Po:P] 「蛇」 d. pa-goh [pa."goh] 「折る（[使]-折れる）」 e. P b77 [P b7] 「葉」 [renders ʔ as P, ˈ as ", ɤ as 7]

new_statements.quote: ムラブリ語は超分節要素 (声調、強勢、母音の長短など) によって語彙を弁別しない。ただし、強勢は音韻語の境界を示す境界表示機能を担う。母音の長短も、常にではないが、強勢を持つ音節にのみ現れうるため、境界表示機能を一部担う。 [...] 音韻語 1 つにつき、1 つの強勢を持つ。強勢位置は音韻語の最終音節である。
new_statements.translation: Mlabri does not distinguish lexical items by suprasegmental features (tone, stress, vowel length, etc.). However, stress carries a demarcative function, marking the boundaries of the phonological word. Vowel length, too, can appear (though not always) only in stressed syllables, and so partly carries a demarcative function. [...] Each phonological word bears one stress. The position of the stress is the final syllable of the phonological word. — Corroborated first-hand by Rischel 1982 ARIPUC 16: 249 (saved file ): 'The minimum rhythmical unit, which is also the typical structure of individual words (lexemes) consists of a stress-syllable with or without a preceding pretonic syllable ("minor syllable", "pre-syllable") ... There are also several lexical items which contain more than one full-vowel syllable. In this case the last syllable seems to have always the main stress ... We are not yet sure about the relevance of degrees of stress (e.g. weak versus secondary stress) on the non-final syllable(s) of a word.'
new_statements.citation: 伊藤雄馬 (Ito, Yuma). 2014. ムラブリ語の文法スケッチ [A grammar sketch of Mlabri]. 地球研言語記述論集 (RIHN Descriptive Linguistics Series) 6: 41-72. Kyoto: Research Institute for Humanity and Nature.
new_statements.locator: §2.2 超分節要素 and §2.3 音韻語, p. 43 (p. 3)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (32 pp., text). p. 3 = printed p. 43 carries §2.2 超分節要素 and §2.3 音韻語. Both quoted sentences are there verbatim: §2.2 "ムラブリ語は超分節要素 (声調、強勢、母音の長短など) によって語彙を弁別しない。ただし、強勢は音韻語の境界を示す境界表示機能を担う。母音の長短も、常にではないが、強勢を持つ音節にのみ現れうるため、境界表示機能を一部担う。" and §2.3 "音韻語 1 つにつき、1 つの強勢を持つ。強勢位置は音韻語の最終音節である。" (the compiler "[..]" only bridges the §2.3 heading). §2.3 goes on to a 2-mora minimal-word constraint with examples boP ["bo:P], tmPoP [tm."Po:P], pa-goh [pa."goh], all stress-final. §3.1 (p. 48, p. 8) confirms the compiler exceptions note: table 10 classifies bound forms by minimal word + stressability (marker +/+, clitic -/+, affix -/-), ex. 5b Pa=w2l [Pa."w2:l ~ "Pa."w2:l], 5c pa-bWl [pa."bW:l], *["pa."bW…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is non-contrastive and demarcative: every phonological word carries exactly one stress, on its final (main) syllable; any preceding pre-syllables (minor syllables) or unstressed full syllables are unstressed, giving the typical Mon-Khmer iambic sesquisyllabic pattern (Ito 2012: 48 states morphemes of 1.5+ syllables 'all show an iambic foot pattern, with stress always on the final syllable of the word').
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not described. Rischel 1982: 249 says the team was 'not yet sure about the relevance of degrees of stress (e.g. weak versus secondary stress) on the non-final syllable(s) of a word'. Ito 2014 mentions only one stress per phonological word.
new_statements.exceptions: Ito 2014 §3.1 (p. 48-49): bound forms differ in stressability — markers and clitics can bear stress (and clitics can form their own phonological word), affixes cannot; e.g. Pa=w2l [Pa.ˈw2:l ~ ˈPa.ˈw2:l]. Rischel 1982: 250 suggests stress and length might be reducible to position in the utterance/phrase (syllable before a major break has strongest stress and longest vowel), but leaves this open.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the phonological word (音韻語), which Ito defines by a minimal-word (2-mora) constraint and stressability; multi-word phrases are not treated. Rischel 1982 is a preliminary phonetic sketch from elicitation in Nan province (citation forms), and notes strong utterance-final lengthening. Bätscher 2015 and the full grammar Rischel 1995 were not opened.
new_statements.identity_note: Ito 2014 explicitly describes the Mlabri 'A dialect' (ムラブリ語 A 方言 = Rischel's Mlabri A / 'Major Mlabri', the larger Nan-province group); Ito 2012 likewise concerns the Thai (Nan) group. Rischel 1982 describes the Nan-province group met on the 1982 Egerod/Theraphan expedition (Rischel's 1995 grammar instead concerns 'Minor Mlabri' = Mlabri B, a small separate group). No separate glottocodes exist for the A/B/C varieties; all fall under mlab1235.

sources.citation: Rischel, Jørgen. 1982. Fieldwork on the Mlabri language: A preliminary sketch of its phonetics. ARIPUC 16: 247-255. DOI 10.7146/aripuc.v16i.131774
sources.note: pp. 249-250: the word = a stress-syllable with or without a preceding pretonic 'pre-syllable'/'minor syllable'; in lexemes with more than one full-vowel syllable 'the last syllable seems to have always the main stress'; unsure about secondary stress on non-final syllables; suggests stress and length may be reducible to phrase position (syllable before a major break is strongest/longest).

sources.citation: 伊藤雄馬 (Ito, Yuma). 2012. ムラブリ語の音声的バリエーションについての予備的調査 [A preliminary survey of phonetic variation in Mlabri]. 地球研言語記述論集 4: 45-60.
sources.note: p. 48: morphemes of 1.5 syllables or more all show an iambic foot pattern, with stress always on the final syllable of the word; stressed syllable = 'main syllable', unstressed light = 'minor syllable', unstressed heavy = 'unstressed syllable'; minor syllables have no stress and show vowel reduction.
